newsitem.title: USA: Quality Food Centers jumps after earnings.
newsitem.headline: Quality Food Centers jumps after earnings.

text.p: Quality Food Centers Inc's stock price jumped after the company reported earnings and sales that were better than expected.
QFC was up 3-11/16 at a 52-week high of 33-3/4.
The company reported earnings of $0.40 a share for its third quarter ended September 7, compared with $0.32 a year earlier and a First Call consensus estimate of $0.37.
An increase in comparable-store sales of 3.4 percent, with no reported food inflation, also beat expectations, said analyst Lesa Sroufe of Ragen MacKenzie.
Sroufe also said the grocery-store chain was boosted by an "upbeat" conference call after the earnings announcement.
"The company reiterated that the Seattle-area economy seems to be helping QFC," she said.
Analysts said the hiring of a former PepsiCo Inc senior executive to head up a new QFC holding company indicates the company plans to expand beyond the Pacific Northwest.
"They're pretty clear that they are going to grow this company fairly dramatically over the next couple of years," said Jonathan Ziegler of Salomon Bros.
He said company executives plan to make acquistions that do not dilute per-share earnings.
